expectations.text: Warns that a proof-heavy editorial-journalists-only policy loses on both value and effort at a developer event.
expectations.evidence: "It costs the most to administer and buys the least developer reach."

expectations.text: States the specific relation: an open policy reaches more of the developer audience than a traditional-outlets-only policy while costing less effort to administer.
expectations.evidence: Same bullet; the recommended policy is the "outlets plus creators" rung.

expectations.text: Explains the effort half: under a proof stack every application must be screened, where an open policy screens nothing.
expectations.evidence: Says "Every application gets screened against a proof stack" but never says an open policy screens nothing.

expectations.text: Explains the value half: a journalists-only policy excludes by definition the constituency that most reliably reaches developers.
expectations.evidence: "Creators, who reach developers most reliably, are excluded by definition."

expectations.text: Recommends one item of proof at this scale, such as links to two recent pieces carrying the applicant's byline, instead of the three-part stack.
expectations.evidence: "a link to two recent pieces with the applicant's byline... Drop the masthead page, the 4–5 articles and the traffic report."

expectations.text: Identifies the quoted proof stack as MWC/GSMA's own published requirements for its own edition, not a standard for a 1,100-person event.
expectations.evidence: "MWC's numbers are MWC's. That policy is built for a far larger press operation."

expectations.text: Confirms the purchased press card is not a credential, citing the published line that a press card alone will not be accepted as press credentials.
expectations.evidence: "A press card alone will not be accepted as press credentials."

expectations.text: Frames declining that applicant as a decision against a published criterion rather than a judgement call, conditional on the criterion having been published first.
expectations.evidence: "Publish before replying... A bar invented after his application reads as invented about him."

expectations.text: Recommends publishing a cap in advance, so that a later refusal is arithmetic rather than a verdict on the applicant.
expectations.evidence: "A published cap turns a later 'no' into arithmetic."

expectations.text: Does not treat last year's one-published-out-of-six as a rate that predicts this year's outcome.
expectations.evidence: It computes "(17%)" and says "A 17% publish rate supports questioning the whole program", treating a six-person sample as a rate.

expectations.text: Names published-versus-accredited as the measurement that actually answers whether the bar is working, and as the input to next edition's comp allocation.
expectations.evidence: "Past performance sets next year's comps. Track published vs. accredited."

expectations.text: Recommends adding a creator lane rather than removing one, with a bar at least as strict as the press lane's.
expectations.evidence: "Hold it to an equal or higher bar than the press lane."
